answer: When an agent submits work, verification clusters spool through a hardened atlas of audited pods, each embedding its signature into a unique hash mapped to a nadir-like root, what determines audit success or failure. Clustering detects timing and wording similarities, and each fake identity must solve a new puzzle costing 2ms per dune-cross correlation at the pod boundary. Attackers pay linear work; delays scale per head, no shortcuts allowed.
